name: Raleigh-Durham International Airport
before:
The airport for the Research Triangle, serving Raleigh, Durham and the surrounding region, and second largest in North Carolina after Charlotte. It set a record in 2025 with 15.6 million passengers.

The connection between terminals is the thing to warn a client about. There is no airside link at all. Moving between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 means leaving security and taking a shuttle bus or the moving walkway through the covered car parks, then clearing again. All international flights without pre-clearance arrive into Terminal 2.

Terminal 1 has nine gates and Terminal 2 the rest, 45 in total.

The airline picture is competitive, which helps fares. Delta has the largest market share and treats it as a focus city, while Breeze Airways flies to more destinations than anyone with 41 and bases aircraft here. Atlanta is the busiest domestic route and New York carries the most passengers a day.

The airport reaches over 90 destinations including 15 international ones across 11 countries, on nearly 600 daily movements. A replacement runway is under construction.
after:
The airport for the Research Triangle, serving Raleigh, Durham and the surrounding region. It is the second largest in North Carolina after Charlotte and set a record in 2025 with 15.6 million passengers.

There are two terminals, each with its own security checkpoint, so check which one a client's airline uses. International flights without US preclearance arrive into Terminal 2.

Terminal 1 has nine gates and Terminal 2 the rest, 45 in total.

Delta has the largest market share, while Breeze Airways, which bases crews here, flies to more destinations than any other airline. Atlanta is the busiest domestic route, though the New York area's airports together carry more passengers.

Counting routes due to start by December 2026, nonstop flights reach more than 90 destinations, 15 of them international in 11 countries. There are nearly 600 aircraft movements a day, and a replacement runway is under construction.

claims.claim: a record 15.6 million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: set a record in 2025 with 15.6 million passengers.
claims.note: Total passengers, arrivals plus departures. The operator's December 2025 report gives 7,834,919 enplaned and 7,814,217 deplaned for the calendar year, 15,649,136 in all (Wikipedia's infobox: 15,644,658); 2024 was 7,746,384 plus 7,726,473, about 15.5 million. The FAA counts 7,670,956 revenue boardings for 2025 (boardings only, about half the total). CONFLICT: the operator's annual report says 'a record 15.7 million people' for calendar 2025, but that is the figure it gives for its fiscal year (April 2025 to March 2026); the operator's own calendar-year statistics round to 15.6 million, so 15.6 is kept.

claims.claim: more than 90 destinations, 15 international in 11 countries, counting routes due by December 2026
claims.inAfter: Counting routes due to start by December 2026, nonstop flights reach more than 90 destinations, 15 of them international in 11 countries.
claims.note: Was 'reaches over 90 destinations including 15 international ones across 11 countries', stated as if all were flying. The operator's list of 'current and scheduled' routes (read 23 Sep 2026) has 91 destinations, five of them starting between October and December 2026. Its 15 international destinations in 11 countries include three of those (Guadalajara on Volaris, Belize and Turks and Caicos on BermudAir); flying today are 86 destinations, 12 of them international in 9 countries. The operator's annual report (year to March 2026) says 'a record 87'.
